attacks.note: Direct INSERT into an allowed table.
attacks.sql: INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, status, ordered_at, total) VALUES (9999, 1, 'paid', CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 1)

attacks.note: Direct DELETE from an allowed table.
MERGE with a destructive matched branch.
attacks.sql: MERGE INTO orders o USING orders s ON o.id = s.id WHEN MATCHED THEN DELETE

attacks.note: SELECT INTO creates and populates a table.

attacks.sql: WITH removed AS (DELETE FROM orders RETURNING id) SELECT * FROM removed
CREATE TABLE copied AS SELECT * FROM orders
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN secret text
GRANT SELECT ON orders TO public
REVOKE SELECT ON orders FROM public

attacks.note: Maintenance command outside the SELECT grammar.
Benign first statement followed by DROP.

attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders LIMIT 1; DELETE FROM orders

attacks.note: SELECT followed by disabling the session timeout.
Allowed projection followed by a denied projection.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM customers LIMIT 1; SELECT email FROM customers

attacks.note: Destructive first statement followed by SELECT.
Empty statement inserted between SELECT and DROP.
Semicolon and DROP are only line-comment text.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders -- ; DROP TABLE orders
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The apparent second statement is inert comment text.

attacks.note: Denied-table text is inside a block comment.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders /* UNION SELECT salary FROM staff_salaries */ ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The denied-table text is inert comment text.

attacks.note: DDL words appear between SELECT and its projection.
attacks.sql: SELECT /* DROP TABLE staff_salaries */ id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The DDL words are inert comment text.

attacks.note: A denied column name is commented out.
attacks.sql: SELECT id /*, email */ FROM customers ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The denied column is not part of the parsed query.

attacks.note: Line-comment and delete tokens appear inside a block comment.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM products /* -- ; DELETE FROM products */ ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
attacks.allowed_to_pass: All attack tokens are inert comment text.

attacks.note: A write is hidden on a commented line.
attacks.sql:
SELECT id FROM products
-- DELETE FROM products
ORDER BY id LIMIT 1
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The write is inert comment text.

attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders /* DROP TABLE orders

attacks.note: Stray comment delimiters surround a stacked write.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders */; DELETE FROM orders; /*

attacks.note: Email projected through a table alias.
attacks.sql: SELECT c.email FROM customers AS c

attacks.note: Case-folding bypass attempt with a quoted denied column.
Denied column propagated through a derived table.
attacks.sql: SELECT email FROM (SELECT email FROM customers) AS private_customer

attacks.note: Denied column hidden behind derived-table star expansion.
attacks.sql: SELECT * FROM (SELECT c.*, c.email FROM customers AS c) AS private_customer

attacks.note: Denied column propagated through a CTE.
attacks.sql: WITH private AS (SELECT email FROM customers) SELECT email FROM private

attacks.note: Correlated denied column projected through LATERAL.
attacks.sql: SELECT x.email FROM customers AS c CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT c.email) AS x

attacks.note: Qualified stars on a join may expose omitted customer columns.
attacks.sql: SELECT c.*, o.* FROM customers AS c JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The validator expands both stars to policy-allowed columns before execution.

attacks.note: Boolean oracle over a denied email.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM customers WHERE email = 'customer001@example.test'

attacks.note: Ordering oracle over a denied email.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM customers ORDER BY email

attacks.note: Grouping oracle over a denied phone number.
attacks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers GROUP BY phone

attacks.note: CASE expression observes a denied phone number.
attacks.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN phone IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END FROM customers

attacks.note: Denied phone used only in a join condition.
attacks.sql: SELECT o.id FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON c.id = o.customer_id AND c.phone LIKE '+90%'

attacks.note: Denied email in one set-operation branch.
attacks.sql: SELECT name FROM customers UNION SELECT email FROM customers

attacks.note: Quoted case variant of a denied table.
Allowed table name in a denied schema.
Three-part table name with an explicit catalog.
Denied table inside a scalar predicate.
attacks.sql: SELECT 1 WHERE 1 IN (SELECT id FROM staff_salaries)
SELECT * FROM (VALUES ((SELECT id FROM staff_salaries))) AS v(id)

attacks.note: TABLE command hidden inside a CTE.
attacks.sql: WITH salaries AS (TABLE staff_salaries) SELECT * FROM salaries

attacks.note: TABLE command used as a predicate source.

attacks.sql: SELECT s.salary FROM customers AS c CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT salary FROM staff_salaries LIMIT 1) AS s

attacks.note: Quoted case trick against a system catalog.

attacks.sql: SELECT c FROM customers AS c

attacks.note: Serialize the physical row including denied columns.
attacks.sql: SELECT row_to_json(c) FROM customers AS c

attacks.sql: SELECT row_to_json(x) FROM (SELECT c FROM customers AS c) AS x

attacks.sql: SELECT id AS c FROM customers AS c ORDER BY c::text

attacks.sql: SELECT id AS customers FROM customers ORDER BY customers::text

SELECT DISTINCT ON (c) id AS c FROM customers AS c

attacks.note: Mutate session configuration through a function.
Import a server-side file as a large object.
Export a large object to a server-side file.
Execute SQL supplied as a string.
Bind parameter instead of a literal LIMIT.

attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders LIMIT ALL

attacks.note: Bind parameter instead of a literal OFFSET.
Huge literal LIMIT should be safely clamped.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 999999999
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The validator rewrites the LIMIT to the configured maximum.

attacks.note: Huge FETCH count should be safely clamped.
attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id FETCH FIRST 999999999 ROWS ONLY
attacks.allowed_to_pass: The validator rewrites FETCH to the configured maximum.

attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id LIMIT 01
attacks.allowed_to_pass: PostgreSQL and the validator treat 01 as the safe literal 1.

attacks.note: Oversized LIMIT in both set-operation branches.
attacks.sql: (SELECT id FROM customers ORDER BY id LIMIT 900) UNION (SELECT customer_id FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id LIMIT 800)
attacks.allowed_to_pass: Every branch is clamped and the outer result receives the default cap.

attacks.sql: SELECT id FROM orders ORDER BY id OFFSET 999999999
attacks.allowed_to_pass: A non-negative literal OFFSET is safe and returns no rows here.

attacks.note: Attempt a huge in-memory string allocation.

attacks.sql: WITH RECURSIVE bomb(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM bomb) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bomb
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders AS a CROSS JOIN orders AS b CROSS JOIN orders AS c

attacks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers AS c CROSS JOIN orders AS o CROSS JOIN order_items AS oi

attacks.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) OVER () FROM order_items AS a CROSS JOIN orders AS b CROSS JOIN products AS c

attacks.note: Aggregate a computed value across a billion-row Cartesian product.
attacks.sql: SELECT SUM(a.total + b.total + c.total) FROM orders AS a CROSS JOIN orders AS b CROSS JOIN orders AS c
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products AS a CROSS JOIN products AS b CROSS JOIN products AS c CROSS JOIN products AS d CROSS JOIN products AS e
